findings.title: Git status contains unauthorized untracked paths
findings.criterion_ref: Critical Criterion 1, “Authorization Boundary Respected”: git status must show only authorized untracked files; execution/P00 permits specific files only.
findings.trigger: Inspecting the current repository with `git status --short --untracked-files=all`.
findings.consequence: P00 cannot satisfy the mandatory zero-unauthorized-path requirement, despite the checkpoint reporting `authorized_paths_only: true`.
findings.evidence: Git status lists `plans_internal/refactor_repo/orchestration/routing_decisions.jsonl`, which is outside every authorized path. It also lists `plans_internal/refactor_repo/execution/P00/p00_execution.log` and `plans_internal/refactor_repo/execution/P00/run_p00.py`; the permitted execution files identified by the artifact’s submission report are only `execution_log.jsonl`, `.execution_log.counter.json`, and `.execution_log.lock`.

observations: `P00_checkpoint_repaired.v1.json` reports `inventory.complete: false`, while the referenced repair inventory at `plans_internal/refactor_repo/inventory/repair_20260816_120500/repository_refactor_inventory.20260816T122829Z.v1.json` reports `complete: true`. This internal inconsistency should be corrected, although the actual inventory’s required completeness field passes.
The repair checkpoint’s `inventory` object does not identify the concrete inventory output path, making linkage less explicit than the baseline linkage.
reasoning: The actual repair inventory reports complete=true with empty omissions and collection failures, and the repair baseline exists with no existing failures. However, the current authoritative git status directly contradicts the checkpoint’s authorization gate and violates a blocker criterion. I did not elevate the checkpoint’s inaccurate inventory summary to a separate finding because the generated inventory JSON itself has the required value.
